title: Ghost Rider
synopsis: Johnny Blaze trades his soul for his father's health. Years after his father's death, the stranger returns to collect by sending Johnny after Blackheart.
verdictRationale: Johnny's love for his father and Mack's care for Johnny are worth admiring. The devil exploits a frightened teenager. Yet the film makes inflicting torment with the Rider’s stare a heroic attraction and lets Johnny keep that power as his answer to evil. That weighs heavily in the proposed verdict.
ageRationale: The dying father's burns, Johnny's frightening transformations and the sight of victims suffering through the stare warrant an older-teen recommendation.
reflection: Mack knows Johnny can survive extraordinary jumps, yet he keeps asking his friend to stop. That quiet act of care offers families a different kind of courage from the one the crowd cheers.

title: Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance
synopsis: Moreau offers Johnny relief from his curse if he gets Danny to safety. The boy’s mother joins the effort to keep him out of Roarke’s hands.
verdictRationale: Nadya sees a child worth protecting when others see a dangerous inheritance. Johnny comes to recognize himself in Danny. Their loyalty is admirable, although the rescue is staged through violent spectacle and a fantasy in which demonic power can be turned to good.
ageRationale: Threats to a child, bodies decaying on contact, burning victims and repeated profanity make the film demanding for younger teens.
reflection: Johnny can offer Danny something before he wins a single fight. He knows what it is to fear that the source of your power determines your future. Speaking to the boy as someone capable of choosing is an act of mercy.

themes.name: Parental love
themes.evidence: Nadya's refusal to abandon Danny sustains the rescue despite repeated attacks.

themes.name: Compassion

themes.name: Exploitation
themes.evidence: Roarke pursues a child in order to use his body, the threat around which the pursuit turns.

title: Daredevil
edition: Original US PG-13 theatrical cut, starring Ben Affleck
synopsis: Matt Murdock offers legal defense by day and pursues suspects as Daredevil by night. His encounter with Elektra brings him into conflict with Bullseye and Kingpin.
verdictRationale: Giving people access to a defense is a real service. The subway death exposes the danger when Matt claims personal authority to punish. His encounters with a priest and a frightened child give viewers reasons to question the satisfaction of seeing an opponent lose.
ageRationale: The subway death has a disturbing aftermath. Other scenes include a stabbing, bloody injuries, a sexual encounter, profanity and a racial slur. Older teens are better placed to discuss the difference between defending victims and exacting revenge.
reflection: A child is frightened by the masked man Matt understands as a protector. In an examination of conscience, that child's judgment deserves room alongside Matt's account of his intentions.

themes.name: Service
themes.evidence: Matt’s pro bono legal work gives people representation and establishes the public vocation against which his night work is measured.

themes.name: Conscience
themes.evidence: His encounter with the priest and the frightened child bring his moral conflict into view in specific scenes.

themes.name: Vigilantism
themes.evidence: Matt's double life rests on his decision to punish where the legal system fails.

themes.name: Cruelty
